response.bodyText: ESA Space News ESA Space News https://www.esa.int/search?subjects=160315 Wed, 25 Nov 2026 01:01:40 +0100 Wed, 25 Nov 2026 01:01:40 +0100 http://blogs.law.harvard.edu/tech/rss space en 600 Copyright European Space Agency rss@esa.int (ESA rss manager) <![CDATA[Euclid breaks own quasar record by 40 million years]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/science/euclid/euclid-breaks-own-quasar-record-by-40-million-years dataobject_161368 The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered the most distant quasar to date: a rare 360 million-sun-mass galactic core seen just 630 million years after the Big Bang. The discovery breaks Euclid’s own previous record, announced only a few months ago[1.1], by peering back in time an additional 40 million years. It also raises a compelling question: how could such an enormous black hole have formed and grown so rapidly after the Big Bang?]]> Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:00:00 +0100 <![CDATA[BepiColombo safely in Mercury orbit despite unexpected challenge ]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/operations/bepicolombo-safely-in-mercury-orbit-despite-unexpected-challenge dataobject_161558 On 21 November, starting at 18:24 UTC, BepiColombo achieved Mercury orbit insertion (MOI), the second major milestone of its planetary arrival phase. As soon as the signal from the spacecraft was re-established after a scheduled loss of contact, the Mission Control Team at the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany, saw that the spacecraft had entered safe mode. An issue occurred during the thruster burn, causing the manoeuvre to end earlier than expected. Since then, teams at ESOC have been working around the clock with lead spacecraft manufacturer Airbus and colleagues across the joint ESA and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) mission to investigate the issue, which has been traced to a software glitch. BepiColombo is safe and in a stable orbit around Mercury – an important milestone after its eight-year journey to the planet – and is on track for the separation of its two science orbiters on 9 December in Germany (10 December in Japan). The mission also delivered a first: entering orbit around another planet using ‘weak stability capture’. This involves arriving at lower speeds than is typical for planetary missions, and is a technique that has previously only been used by some spacecraft travelling to Earth's moon. ]]> Mon, 23 Nov 2026 19:00:00 +0100 <![CDATA[Hera’s Didymos asteroid in eclipse]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/operations/space-safety/hera/hera-s-didymos-asteroid-in-eclipse dataobject_161548 A solar eclipse in deep space, shown in this early view of the Didymos binary asteroids from the European Space Agency’s Hera mission for planetary defence. The smaller Dimorphos moonlet is seen casting its shadow across part of its Didymos parent body, to blank out the Sun across the shaded stretch of rocky surface.]]> Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:10:46 +0100 <![CDATA[Rain breaks up Earth’s natural sunshades]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/earth-observation-programmes/futureeo/earthcare/rain-breaks-up-earth-s-natural-sunshades dataobject_161524 EarthCARE sheds light on one of the processes that leads to the breakup of vast, bright clouds that help keep our planet cool – with rain emerging as a key driver.]]> Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0100 <![CDATA[Watch live: Hera’s first images of post-impact asteroid Dimorphos]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/operations/space-safety/hera/watch-live-hera-s-first-images-of-post-impact-asteroid-dimorphos dataobject_161518 A little more than four years ago, humans moved an asteroid, as NASA’s DART spacecraft impacted a body called Dimorphos. Now the European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft has arrived at that same asteroid to find out what happened next. Join the Hera team on the evening of Wednesday 25 November as they share the first close-up images of this historic transformed space object.]]> Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:10:00 +0100 <![CDATA[Seven-spacecraft observatory to study plasma universe]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/science/seven-spacecraft-observatory-to-study-plasma-universe dataobject_161527 ESA Member States have selected Plasma Observatory as the agency’s next medium-class mission. Its seven coordinated spacecraft will track how the Sun’s energy moves through Earth’s magnetic shield, across different scales of distance and time.]]> Thu, 19 Nov 2026 00:00:00 +0100 <![CDATA[First thermal images from Sentinel-3C radiometer]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/earth-observation-programmes/copernicus/sentinel-3/first-thermal-images-from-sentinel-3c-radiometer dataobject_161507 These are the first images showing land- and sea-surface temperatures from the third satellite of the Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission, Sentinel-3C. ]]> Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:00:00 +0100 <![CDATA[In the shadow of volcanic giants]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/science/mars-express/in-the-shadow-of-volcanic-giants dataobject_161506 Even Mars’s more modest volcanoes demand attention. This month’s snapshot from ESA’s Mars Express spotlights Tharsis Tholus, a fascinating peak with an eventful past.]]> Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:00:00 +0100 <![CDATA[Prodex at 40: advancing European space science]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/prodex-at-40-advancing-european-space-science dataobject_161438 For forty years, Prodex, the European Space Agency’s Programme for the Development of Scientific Experiments, has turned the scientific ambitions of its Participating States into instruments and experiments flown in space.]]> Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:03:28 +0100 <![CDATA[Hera surveying asteroids with superhuman vision]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/operations/space-safety/hera/hera-surveying-asteroids-with-superhuman-vision dataobject_161478 The European Space Agency’s Hera mission for planetary defence surveys its target asteroids with a combination of instruments, peering beyond the limits of the human eye. The larger Didymos asteroid – dominated by its dramatic equatorial ridge – is seen here from just 28.5 km away, variously in visible light, multispectral and thermal infrared vision.]]> Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:59:44 +0100 <![CDATA[Hera spies a half-hidden asteroid moonlet]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/operations/space-safety/hera/hera-spies-a-half-hidden-asteroid-moonlet dataobject_161422 Another early preview of the Didymos binary asteroid system from ESA’s Hera mission for planetary defence. Acquired from 56 km away, this image shows one face of the main 730-m-diameter Didymos asteroid. A small part of its 151-m-diameter Dimorphos moonlet is also visible, peeking out from near the top of Didymos.]]> Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:04:40 +0100 <![CDATA[Euclid lays the foundation for its best-ever 3D map of the Universe]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/science/euclid/euclid-lays-the-foundation-for-its-best-ever-3d-map-of-the-universe dataobject_161010 The European Space Agency’s Euclid mission has released its first major batch of data. With this release, which captures the light of more than a billion objects and covers an area of sky as big as 9500 full Moons, ESA’s dark Universe detective lays the foundation for its largest-ever 3D map of the cosmos.]]> Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:00:00 +0100 <![CDATA[Hera spacecraft in ‘rectangular orbit’ around target asteroids]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/operations/space-safety/hera/hera-spacecraft-in-rectangular-orbit-around-target-asteroids dataobject_161349 The European Space Agency’s Hera mission for planetary defence has arrived at its target asteroids. Positioned just 30-25 km away from the binary Didymos system, the small-car-sized spacecraft has commenced its ‘early characterisation phase’ to gather key data on the asteroid pair.]]> Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:00:00 +0100 <![CDATA[Predicting El Niño's impact on carbon sinks ]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/earth-observation-programmes/futureeo/space-for-our-climate/predicting-el-nino-s-impact-on-carbon-sinks dataobject_161379 Satellite observations across the central-eastern Pacific, combined with seasonal climate forecasts, are pointing to the development of one of the strongest El Niño events in recent decades – and offer early insights into where the land’s ability to absorb and store carbon could be most at risk. ]]> Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:30:00 +0100 <![CDATA[MTG-I2 weather satellite delivers first images]]> https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/earth-observation-programmes/meteorological-missions/meteosat-third-generation/mtg-i2-weather-satellite-delivers-first-images dataobject_161325 The Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) mission’s second Imager satellite has delivered its first images, showing weather patterns over Europe and Africa. ]]> Fri, 06 Nov 2026 12:15:00 +0100
